title: 2015 AMC 12A Problem 6
statement: Two years ago Pete was three times as old as his cousin Claire. Two years before that, Pete was four times as old as Claire. In how many years will the ratio of their ages be \(2 : 1?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(p\) and \(c\) be Pete’s and Claire’s current ages. Then \(p-2 = 3(c-2)\) and \(p-4 = 4(c-4).\)

Solving these gives \(p = 20\) and \(c = 8,\) so Pete is \(12\) years older than Claire.

The ratio is \(2 : 1\) when Claire is \(12,\) which is \(12 - 8 = 4\) years from now.

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Let \(p,c\) be their current ages: \(p-2=3(c-2)\) and \(p-4=4(c-4)\)
Solve for \(p\) and \(c,\) then find \(n\) with \(p+n = 2(c+n)\)
